review_notes: Read the whole file, plus D2Y4 (E9_data) and D2Y9 (Good.E9, zpowers_conj_z). Findings are the repeated rk4/rk6 argument (also in D2Y9), the repeated "two order-3 elements generate centR" block (here twice, plus D2Y9), and the repeated conjugation of a product of powers. I did not check whether D2Y9 imports can be reordered. I only know D2Y9 imports D2Y7, as D2Y8 does, so a shared lemma would have to sit in D2Y7 or in a small new file. I did not report the two copies of the `hr'` normalizer step (kerMod.inv_mem' and conj_mem_kerMod), because they are only 3 lines each. Nothing was compiled; the proposed lemmas are sketches.

findings.problem: normalizes_Z_of_RP re-proves, line for line, the rank-contradiction argument already in D2Y9.zpowers_conj_z. Both show that a nontrivial conjugate of z lying in centR X x generates the same subgroup as z. Both first prove q*z*q⁻¹ ≠ 1 with the same `z = q⁻¹ * (q*z*q⁻¹) * q` trick. Then both call hg.rk4, rewrite with rk_commV_zpowers_conj, and finish with hg.rk6 and omega. normalizes_Z_of_RP only adds a by_contra wrapper around zpowers equality, so the core is two copies of the same reasoning. The same non-triviality step is also repeated in tinv_centralizes_z, lines 169–173.
findings.proposed_change: Move zpowers_conj_z, stated for `Good X t x z` and a single conjugator q with `hconj : q * z * q⁻¹ ∈ centR X x`, to a place both files can import (D2Y7 or a small new file; D2Y9 imports D2Y7). It is proved once with the rk4/rk6 argument. Then normalizes_Z_of_RP becomes: build hconj as now, then `(Subgroup.mem_zpowers_iff ...)` or `by rw [← zpowers_conj_z hg hconj]; exact Subgroup.mem_zpowers _`. A conjugate-of-1 lemma (`q * z * q⁻¹ = 1 → z = 1`, available from `conj_eq_one_iff`-style API or stated once) replaces the manual `group` block at 148–153 and 169–173.
findings.benefit: The rank-4/rank-6 counting argument is stated and maintained once. A change to the Good hypotheses (rk4/rk6) no longer has to be applied to three places across two files.

findings.excerpt:
have hle : Subgroup.zpowers l ⊔ Subgroup.zpowers z ≤ centR X x :=
    sup_le (Subgroup.zpowers_le.mpr hlP) (Subgroup.zpowers_le.mpr hg.hz)
  have heq : Subgroup.zpowers l ⊔ Subgroup.zpowers z = centR X x :=
    Subgroup.eq_of_le_of_card_ge hle (by rw [hEcard, hg.card])
findings.problem: The same argument occurs in refl_mod_z (196–201), in D2_29 (265–270, lines 266–269 being the sup_le / eq_of_le_of_card_ge part), and in D2Y9.Good.E9 (54–57). It takes two commuting order-3 elements a, b in centR X x with distinct zpowers. It applies E9_data to get card 9, shows the join lies in centR X x via sup_le, and concludes equality from hg.card. Only then does it extract the `a^i * b^j` form. Each instance repeats this reasoning with different variable names.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma, e.g. `Good.centR_eq_sup (hg : Good X t x z) {a b} (ha : a ∈ centR X x) (hb : b ∈ centR X x) (hao : orderOf a = 3) (hbo : orderOf b = 3) (hab : a * b = b * a) (hne : zpowers a ≠ zpowers b) : zpowers a ⊔ zpowers b = centR X x ∧ ∀ y ∈ centR X x, ∃ i j : ℤ, y = a ^ i * b ^ j`. The proof is: obtain hEcard and hform from E9_data; sup_le gives ≤; Subgroup.eq_of_le_of_card_ge with `rw [hEcard, hg.card]` gives =; the second part rewrites with heq. In refl_mod_z it replaces 196–202 with one `obtain ⟨heq, hform⟩`, and `hr'` is then `hform r (by rw [hRP]; exact hr)`. In D2_29 it replaces 265–271 similarly with `hform z hg.hz`. Good.E9 in D2Y9 can reuse it too (D2Y9 would need this lemma in a file it imports).
findings.benefit: The three proofs shrink by about 6–7 lines each and read as 'centR is generated by a, b'. The card/containment argument has a single point of maintenance. It also shows that the repeated hform use is really 'every element of centR has the form a^i b^j'.

      _ = (t' * l * t'⁻¹) ^ i * (t' * z * t'⁻¹) ^ j := by rw [← conj_zpow, ← conj_zpow]
findings.problem: refl_mod_z (206–209) and D2_29 (274–279) both prove the same distribution identity. It is conjugation of a product of two integer powers, `t*(a^i*b^j)*t⁻¹ = (t*a*t⁻¹)^i * (t*b*t⁻¹)^j`, by splitting with `group` and applying conj_zpow twice. It is then specialised using known conjugates. The identical 3-step calc is written twice, with different variable names.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma `conj_mul_zpow_zpow (t a b : MulAut V) (i j : ℤ) : t * (a ^ i * b ^ j) * t⁻¹ = (t * a * t⁻¹) ^ i * (t * b * t⁻¹) ^ j`, proved by `rw [← conj_zpow, ← conj_zpow]; group` (or by the existing calc). Then hconj in refl_mod_z becomes `by rw [conj_mul_zpow_zpow, hinv, htz]`, and h1 in D2_29 becomes `by rw [hij, conj_mul_zpow_zpow, hinv₁, hp₂.hinv]`. This could be combined with the previous finding's lemma or conj_zpowers_mem near the top of section Main.
findings.benefit: This removes two 3–4 line calcs and their repeated `group` rewrite shape. The two proofs then read as 'conjugate each factor, substitute', so the real content is the substituted relations.
